messages:
acme-sysadmin: we're seeing intermittent NXDOMAIN for service endpoint 'api.internal.acme' from pods in prod VPC after tenant onboarding, started ~0400 UTC :confused:
acme-sysadmin: curl inside pod just returns 'Could not resolve host: api.internal.acme'
acme-sysadmin: dig +short api.internal.acme @10.0.0.2 -> (nothing) NXDOMAIN
acme-sysadmin: this worked yesterday, no deploys in the last 24h on their side
support_amy: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste dig +trace from a failing node? also which account/region is the VPC in?
acme-sysadmin: region us-east-1, account 987654321, dig +trace attached:
```
;; global options: +cmd
.                       518400.00 IN NS a.root-servers.net.
...
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
acme-sysadmin: also tried nslookup vs node-local (169.254.20.10) -> NXDOMAIN
infra_bot: route53 change detected: new private hosted zone 'internal.acme' created in account 123456789 and associated with vpc-0a1b2c3d in us-east-1 at 2026-03-16T03:59:10Z
acme-sysadmin: oh that might be it — we have service endpoints in our account that rely on private hosted zone in tenant account, could be split-horizon overlap
support_amy: copy — can you confirm the hosted zone IDs and whether the VPC is associated to both hosted zones? run: aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-0a1b2c3d --region us-east-1
acme-sysadmin: ran it, returned two hosted zones with same name, different IDs. one is ours (HZ-A) and one created by partner (HZ-B). VPC is associated to both.
eng_sre_jordan: associating two private hosted zones with the same name to the same VPC causes split-horizon and unpredictable responses — route53 returns arbitrary zone depending on internal allocation :thinking:
eng_sre_jordan: that can produce NXDOMAIN if the wrong zone lacks the SRV/A record for the service endpoint
acme-sysadmin: confirmed A record present in HZ-A but missing in HZ-B (partner's). that explains missing records.
ops_mike: quick mitigation: disassociate the partner's hosted zone from the VPC or add the missing records in their hosted zone. which org owns HZ-B?
acme-sysadmin: HZ-B is in account 123456789 (partner-managed). they created it during onboarding automation.
support_amy: asked partner to either disassociate HZ-B from our VPC or delegate DNS. asked to add record as temporary fix.
acme-sysadmin: note: some pods did resolve correctly (probabilistic) leading to intermittent api errors and TLS cert validation failures because CNAME pointed at internal lb with different cert -> app-level errors and increased 5xxs
eng_sre_jordan: yep TLS errors line up with hitting wrong backend. add short-term workaround: set node /etc/hosts in a debug node or put a stub resolver rule pointing to correct IP, but better to fix hosted zone association.
support_amy: can you share output of tcpdump udp port 53 from a failing pod? want to confirm query path and response flags
acme-sysadmin: tcpdump shows queries to node-local (169.254.20.10) then to 10.0.0.2, responses TTL 0 and RCODE=3 (NXDOMAIN)
support_amy: RCODE=3 confirms name exists in some zone but no matching RRset, consistent with duplicate HZ where one lacks record
infra_bot: policy alert: cross-account hosted zone association detected without explicit allowlist. ticket created INC-2026-1122
support_amy: escalation next step: i'll open an internal support ticket to infra to request: 1) verify VPC associations for both HZ IDs, 2) confirm whether onboarding automation should be prevented from auto-associating HZs, 3) recommend resolution path (disassociate HZ-B or add missing records)
support_amy: acme-sysadmin, while we triage can you confirm if using the public API endpoint (if available) or hitting the dedicated IP works as temporary fallback?
acme-sysadmin: public endpoint works for now but routing has higher latency; customers notice timeouts in some flows
eng_sre_jordan: after partner disassociated HZ-B from VPC the NXDOMAINs stopped for us. please keep monitoring, but root cause is duplicate private hosted zone association causing split-horizon. we'll follow up to harden onboarding automation.
acme-sysadmin: confirmed resolution — NXDOMAIN gone, TLS errors resolved, thanks :raised_hands:
support_amy: closing loop — created follow-up to product to add a guardrail preventing cross-account private HZ auto-assoc to customer VPCs unless explicit trust established. tagging infra and onboarding teams.
ops_mike: reminder for runbook add: how to detect duplicate HZs quickly: run aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name internal.acme --region us-east-1 and list-hosted-zones-by-vpc for associations
eng_sre_jordan: add note: check node-local cache and kube-dns/ CoreDNS config; sometimes node-local caches stale NXDOMAINs — clear cache if you recently fixed association
support_amy: thanks everyone — marking thread resolved but will keep ticket open for onboarding automation fix.
